text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday as reported by the official Algerian news agency APS. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government reports $2.23 billion trade surplus in the first nine months of 1996.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia says in a campaign rally in Algiers the November 28 referendum to change the constitution will shut the door for carpetbagger politicians.

- Businessmen from Qatar and United Arab Emirates to invest in Algeria, mostly in building an international trade center, a hospital and a highway linking the eastern town of Annaba to western city of Oran.

- Air Algerie denies it will resume flights to Paris airport in 1997 as reported by the Algerian ambassador in France. The national airline suspended its operations in Paris in 1995 in a row with French aviation authorities over a terminal transfer.
